slides.author: Alexey Grigorev
slides.title: Agent traces rarely arrive as clean tables
slides.subtitle: They arrive as nested JSON. Schema design becomes part of observability.

slides.title: The first pipeline created 78 tables
slides.body: dlt normalized the trace files into relational tables. The high table count came from deeply nested messages, usage, cache, models, and tool data.

slides.title: This is expected
slides.body: Nested JSON has structure. Loading it into a relational destination requires choices about how much to flatten.

slides.title: Schema pollution is real
slides.body: Flatten everything and the schema can explode. Keep too much raw JSON and important fields become harder to query.

slides.title: The adjusted schema had 40 tables
slides.body: The agent kept selected fields as JSON columns. The result was a more manageable schema while preserving useful structure.

slides.supportingText: A practical data engineering lesson inside an agent traces demo.
